extracted.intended_audience: SNSF policymakers, program evaluators, funding-agency stakeholders, and researchers interested in Ambizione outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying the evaluation criteria and metrics used in the SNSF Ambizione final evaluation report to judge the scheme's reach, implementation, and impacts on grantees' careers and scientific independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding share for doctoral students/postdocs/other personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Who finances doctoral students, postdocs and other personnel (Ambizione grant vs host institution). The report shows proportions (e.g. ~30% of doctoral students financed fully by host; for postdocs host obliged to finance at least 50% of salary; 11% of postdocs: host financed more than 50%; almost 20% fully financed by host; other personnel: 18% financed fully by host, ~49% fully by Ambizione).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the percentages from grantee survey and note contractual obligations (host must finance >=50% of a hired postdoc). Interpret split funding (shared funding) and full host-financing as indicators of host commitment; report also notes source: Interface online survey. Include explicit percentages when assessing scheme implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching activities engagement and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which Ambizione grantees engage in teaching (66% did), typical hours taught per week per semester (most taught one (24%), two (17%), or four (15%) hours including prep), at which course levels (Bachelor’s, Master’s, Doctoral), and how teaching was financed (Table 8: fully through Ambizione 47%, partially Ambizione/host 11%, fully host 19%, other 6%, don't know 18%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating burden and role balance, report share engaged in teaching, hours distribution, course levels, and funding source. Note survey data caveat: many outliers suggest the 'hours per week per semester' question was sometimes misunderstood and results should be treated cautiously. Also note the report that there is no conceivable correlation between hours taught and financing model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach of target groups (returning, incoming, limited mobility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Ambizione reaches the intended target groups. SNSF application database classification shows distribution among grantees since 2008: Returning 53% (163), Incoming 43% (132*), Limited mobility 4% (13) (total 308).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use complete application-database classification as a primary metric for reach. Note classification is done manually using self-reported indicators and may be biased; see annex for category definitions. Report trends over time (e.g. increasing popularity among foreign researchers) and small size of limited-mobility group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness among eligible researchers and reasons for non-application
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of whether eligible target groups know of Ambizione (83% of comparison group 2 had heard of it) and the self-reported reasons why eligible researchers did not apply (Table 10: did not meet participation requirements 38%, SNSF project funding better suited 30%, Ambizione not appealing 10%, couldn't find a host 1%, did not feel scientifically independent 1%, other reasons 34%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report awareness rates from surveys and enumerate ranked reasons for non-application. Note multiple responses were possible. Qualitatively interpret 'other' reasons (e.g. already in stable positions, applied later, or scheme did not yet exist). Use this to assess accessibility and attractiveness of the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of grantees and experts with the scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings from interviews: experts and former grantees generally expressed high satisfaction; Ambizione particularly suited for returnees and helps reintegration; foreigners value grant sum but may face difficulties finding Swiss positions post-funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative interview evidence to assess perceived strengths (reintegration help, grant attractiveness) and contextual limitations (Swiss labor market constraints). Include expert observations such as the perception of Ambizione as often seen as a stepping stone to SNSF professorships and potential age/career-timing implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on scientific independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether Ambizione increases grantees' scientific independence: experts saw Ambizione as effective in boosting independence and as a 'label' enhancing competitiveness; it protects grantees from teaching duties. Limitations noted: Ambizione status does not formally allow PhD supervision; grant duration often too short for PhD completion; experts suggested allowing parallel SNSF project funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both perceived positive effects (protected time, label effect) and structural limitations (supervision rights, duration). Consider recommendations (e.g. permit parallel project funding) when judging scheme's capacity to create genuine scientific independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on career development and employability
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured impact on grantees' careers: interview and survey evidence that Ambizione contributed to career steps (examples of full/associate/assistant professors, SNSF professors, group leaders), continuity of employment after the grant (e.g. of 70 former grantees 86% employed and 97% still in science), and that Ambizione helped obtain further funding (SNSF professorships, ERC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both survey percentages and illustrative interview anecdotes to assess career influence. Report distribution of current positions (Figure 7, Table 13), gender/discipline breakdowns, and note small sample caveats. Consider comparison groups to contextualize effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey-measured effects on research outputs and profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit survey dimensions measured (Figure 4): improved competence in research field (96%), enhanced scientific profile (96%), increased scientific competitiveness (92%), increased number of scientific publications (81%), improved networking (73%), improved quality of scientific publications (percentages smaller), easier access to leading scientists, and enabling return to Swiss science scene (variable by subgroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these listed effects as discrete evaluation metrics; report overall agreement rates and disaggregate by field and gender when available (e.g. female respondents reported higher gains in networking and access to leading scientists). Use these metrics to compare perceived benefits of Ambizione versus other funding types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of effects with SNSF project funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey of comparison group 2 (SNSF project funding beneficiaries) showed very similar self-assessed effects (e.g. enhanced profile 94%, increased competitiveness 93%, improved competence 92%), indicating many effects are not unique to Ambizione.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct comparisons with project funding to identify Ambizione-specific impacts versus common effects of SNSF funding generally. Report where Ambizione differs (e.g. enabling return to Swiss scene) and where effects are similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadweight effect (would project have proceeded without Ambizione)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of potential deadweight: Ambizione grantees self-reported 36% could have conducted their project without the grant; rejected applicants (comparison group 1) responses imply a deadweight effect up to 51% when including those who could do the project to a smaller extent; only 17% would definitely have done it without funding (complete deadweight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish complete vs partial deadweight. Use comparison groups (rejected applicants) to validate grantees' self-reports and to provide a more conservative estimate. Interpret 36–51% in relation to benchmarks from similar funding schemes and discuss acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment outcome metrics vs comparison groups (professorship and long-term positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative comparison of current positions after grant: Ambizione former postdocs -> 58% became professors after funding vs 25% in rejected applicants; share in long-term-perspective positions highest among Ambizione grantees (30%) compared to SNSF project beneficiaries (24%) and rejected applicants (17.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these comparative outcome rates as evidence of Ambizione's positive career impact. Report exact figures from Table 14 and discuss sample-size and group-size limitations when drawing causal inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components/definitions of scientific independence (field-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-ended survey responses compiled into common components by field (Table 15). Humanities & social sciences: ability to conduct own research project and choose methods, freedom to publish as sole/first/last author, raise funds/manage budget, establish networks, supervise personnel. Math & natural engineering: freedom to choose research focus, publish independently, acquire funding, supervise PhD/postdocs, initiate collaborations, develop original ideas, be invited to conferences. Biology & medicine: publish as senior/last author, develop own questions, lead research group and supervise, choose personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these listed components as operationalizations of 'scientific independence' that vary by discipline. Use them to design discipline-specific indicators (publication authorship role, grant acquisition, supervisory responsibility, lab leadership, network/visibility metrics) when assessing independence outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label effect and signaling on the job market
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione acts as a 'label' that boosts competitiveness on the academic job market (experts and interviewees reported that holding Ambizione gives a stand-alone advantage against many applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating the scheme's non-monetary benefits, measure reputational/signaling effects via survey questions, anecdotal evidence (e.g. competition statements), and subsequent success in competitive appointments or grant awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural/institutional limitations affecting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual constraints that limit Ambizione's impact: limited number of tenure-track positions in Switzerland causing grantees to seek positions abroad; Ambizione status not granting formal rights to supervise PhD students; short funding duration often too short for PhD completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include systemic labor-market constraints and institutional status limitations in any appraisal of the scheme; distinguish which barriers are attributable to Ambizione design and which are external (national job market). Consider recommended policy responses (e.g. allowing parallel project funding) in evaluation.
